notes:
Short summary: Silverquill builds a native IDE copilot (VS Code + internal cloud IDE) used by ~400 active devs. Evaluating Redwood Private in air-gapped mode to replace current unreliable on-prem microservice. Primary must-haves: low token streaming latency for IDE-like UX, predictable throughput for 150-200 concurrent devs, offline model update workflow, strong audit/KMS, and a packaging format they can sign and scan before installing.

From discovery call (Maya + Liam with CTO, Security lead): 'We cannot accept any outbound network from the inference host; model bundles must be signed and delivered via USB or internal artifact repo.'

Technical priorities:
- Latency target: median per-token generation latency <= 30-50ms end-to-end for small completions (preferred 30ms).
- Throughput: support ~200 concurrent low-latency streams with tail p95 latency under 200ms.
- Model strategy: start with a quantized 7B / 13B family variant for fast local inference; want clear model pinning and rollback semantics; ability to ship delta updates (patch tarballs) for tokenizers and model weights.
- Packaging: air-gapped installer (tar.gz) + signed model packages; offline package validation CLI; MD5/SHA and signature verification documented.
- Hardware: customer lab has 2x H100 nodes (80GB) and 8x A30 capacity; they prefer sizing guidance that fits within those constraints or a recommended temporary rental for stress tests.
- Ops: retention controls for request logs, secure KV cache clearing between sessions, and integration to their on-prem KMS/HSM for keys.

Business posture: cost-sensitive on per-seat economics but willing to commit to Dedicated/Private contract if latency/packaging guarantees met. They are particularly worried about future monthly maintenance and model update cadence in air-gap mode.

Quoted items: security checklist and air-gap packaging spec requested 2026-01-25 (sent), pricing deck v2 in Drive.

CRM shorthand: POC = air-gap installer -> lab deploy -> perf run -> security signoff -> procurement.

Callouts: ask Eng team to include a short demo script for low-latency streaming from VS Code extension and a short note on how KV cache warming will work in a cold-start POC.
